The house

A taproom that was a home first

Fill's opened in 2015 in celebration of craft beer — a family-owned taproom inside a hundred-year-old craftsman a block off Cole Street. The rooms are still rooms: leather chesterfields by the window, an Edison-lit bar under a marquee that just says BEER, and one navy wall of white tile with all the handles in a row.

It pours like a bottle shop and sits like a living room — a pint, a flight, or something for the road, and nobody's in a hurry to turn your table.

Out front

Something's usually parked on the lawn

Fill's doesn't run a kitchen. It runs a front yard — food trucks pull up, bands set up, and the turf fills in.

Food trucks

Burgers, Thai, pizza — Stacks Burgers and Khun 9 Thai have both parked here. [PLACEHOLDER — ask client: this month's truck schedule]

Live music

Local acts on the lawn when the weather cooperates and inside when it doesn't — Kaitie Wade played the house last fall. [PLACEHOLDER — ask client: upcoming shows]

Bring your own

Outside food is welcome — order something, grab a table under the umbrellas, and bring the dog. Root beer's on tap for the kids.
